phase1.intro:
throw and throws look almost identical but do completely different jobs.

Which one first?

dialogue: [[term:throw]] is a statement — it goes INSIDE a method body, and it actively creates and raises an exception right then and there: `throw new IllegalArgumentException("Amount cannot be negative!");`.
The moment that line runs, execution stops dead and jumps to the nearest matching catch (or up the call stack if there isn't one).

stickyNote.flavor: ⚡ creates and raises an exception, right now
stickyNote.definition: throw new SomeException(...); is a statement inside a method that immediately raises an exception, stopping execution at that point.

topics.buttonText: What does throws mean on a method signature?
dialogue: [[term:throws]], with an "s", is part of a method's SIGNATURE: `public void withdraw(double amount) throws Exception`. It doesn't throw anything itself — it's a warning label saying "calling me might result in this exception."
[[key:throw creates and raises one specific exception, right now; throws declares a possibility, for whoever calls this method to plan around]].

stickyNote.flavor: 🏷️ a warning label on the method signature
stickyNote.definition: throws Exception in a method signature declares a possibility a caller must handle or re-declare — it doesn't raise anything itself.

topics.buttonText: Can I throw anything, like a String?
dialogue: [[warn:throw only ever accepts a genuine Throwable object]] — never a String, an int, or anything else. `throw "error!";` simply isn't legal Java; you always need `throw new SomeException("error!");`.

stickyNote.flavor: 🚫 no Strings, no ints — a real exception object
stickyNote.definition: throw only accepts an actual Throwable object, constructed with new — you can never throw a bare String or primitive.

phase2.errorMessage:
Validator.java:5: error: incompatible types: String cannot be converted to Throwable
            throw "Age cannot be negative!";  // Wrong!
            ^
1 error
phase2.explanation:
throw "Age cannot be negative!"; is trying to throw a plain String — and Java only lets you throw genuine Throwable objects (Exception, Error, or one of their subclasses). A String has no idea how to be caught, hold a stack trace, or do anything an exception needs to do.

[[key:always construct a real exception object before throwing it]] — new IllegalArgumentException("Age cannot be negative!") is a Throwable; the bare String never was.

Also worth flagging while we're here: [[warn:throw new IllegalArgumentException(); with no message]] compiles fine but leaves whoever catches it with nothing to go on. A message costs nothing and saves real debugging time later — always give your exceptions something meaningful to say.
phase2.openingDialogue: Watch what happens when you try to throw something that isn't an exception~

phase3.openingDialogue: Let's declare a possibility, then actually raise it~

mcq.question:
Which statement correctly distinguishes throw from throws?

A) throw goes in a method signature; throws goes inside the method body
B) throw actively creates and raises an exception; throws declares that a method might raise one
C) throw and throws do the exact same thing
D) throws can only be used with unchecked exceptions

phase4.selfChallenge:
Create a class Product with:
• Fields: name (String), price (double)
• Constructor with validation:
  - If name is null or empty → throw IllegalArgumentException
  - If price < 0 → throw IllegalArgumentException
• Method: getDiscountedPrice(double discount) that:
  - If discount < 0 or > 50 → throw IllegalArgumentException
  - Returns price * (1 - discount/100)

In main, test with valid and invalid inputs.

phase5.trivia: [[fun:Fun fact]]: the requirement that throw only accepts a genuine Throwable — never a raw String or error code — is a deliberate design choice: by forcing every error to be a real object, Java guarantees every exception automatically carries a stack trace, a message, and a type you can catch specifically, instead of every developer inventing their own ad-hoc error-signaling convention.
phase5.openingDialogue: One more thought before you go~
